title: An Owl Turns Its Head 270 Degrees. Why Doesn't That Kill It?

scenes.text: An owl can look behind itself without moving its body. Why doesn't that kill it?
Its head can turn up to two hundred seventy degrees in either direction.
Twist your own neck that far and the arteries pinch shut. Blood stops reaching the brain.
Scientists at Johns Hopkins scanned twelve owls to find the trick.
Its neck arteries have extra slack, bony channels ten times wider than the vessels, and little blood reservoirs that keep the brain fed.
So the owl keeps staring, and its brain never goes without blood.

description:
An owl can turn its head up to 270 degrees without cutting off blood to the brain.
Johns Hopkins researchers found extra-slack arteries, wide bony channels and blood reservoirs in the neck.
Could you look behind you like that?
first_comment: If you could turn your head like an owl, what would you do with it?
